newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Fresh Taleban fighters pour into Kabul - radio.
newsitem.headline: Fresh Taleban fighters pour into Kabul - radio.

text.p: Hundreds of fresh fighters arrived in the Afghan capital Kabul on Tuesday to help the Taleban Islamic movement's government fight its opponents, the official Kabul Radio said.

The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, said the volunteers came from the eastern province of Paktia and surrounding areas and belonged to the Ahmadzai tribe, like former communist president Najibullah whom the Taleban executed soon after capturing Kabul on September 27.
"They were deployed to positions and posts wherever needed," the radio said.

It said Jalaluddin Haqqani, a prominent guerrilla commander during the war against Soviet occupation in the 1980s, also arrived in Kabul on Tuesday with his Ahmadzai fighters and met the minority Shi'ite Moslem community in western Kabul.
The Taleban movement, which is dominated by the majority Sunni Moslem Pashtuns, is also daily sending volunteers from southern Afghanistan to Kabul, Taleban sources in Pakistan said on Monday.

They said the volunteers were being sent from the main southern town of Kandahar, the Taleban headquarters. They said more than 200 militia fighters injured in fighting north of Kabul had also been brought to Kandahar for medical treatment.
"Hundreds are leaving daily," a Taleban spokesman in the southwestern Pakistani town of Quetta, Mullah Juma Khan Akhund, told Reuters.
He said the Taleban need not make an effort to recruit people to fight what he called a Jihad (holy war).
"It is jihad, people come voluntarily to join it," he said.
